  • How to forge powerful partnerships to implement change
  • How to measure and scale what works

course_description:
This course provides public sector professionals with a comprehensive understanding of Generative AI (GenAI) and its potential to revolutionize work in government. Through hands-on activities and best practices, participants learn to use GenAI as a powerful companion to assist in their daily tasks while maintaining public trust and safety. The course covers the fundamentals of GenAI, its practical applications, prompt engineering techniques, risk mitigation strategies, and broader societal challenges. By the end of the course, participants will be equipped to harness the power of GenAI responsibly and effectively in their public sector roles.

InnovateUS is partnering with public sector organizations nationwide to roll out the course for public professionals, including but not limited to the State of California, the State of New Jersey, Miami-Dade County/Community College, and the State of Maryland.  The training will be hosted on InnnovateUS’s learning management system (LMS). However, those from select public sector organizations will be able to access the course through their state’s own LMS.
course_learnings:
Divided into short accessible videos, the course is designed to give you practical skills you can use to serve the public better.

  • Introduction to GenAI: Master the fundamentals of Generative AI
  • Public Sector Uses: Explore real-world cases where GenAI is improving government services
  • Essential Tools: Master key GenAI platforms and how to use them in your work in government
  • Security & Ethics: Learn best practices for protecting sensitive information while using GenAI
  • Critical Perspectives: Understand key societal risks and opportunities created by AI
short_description: This free, self-paced online course helps you integrate GenAI tools into your government work, enhancing public service delivery while managing risks responsibly.

resource_modules.module_title: Module 2: Explaining Generative AI: What it is
resource_modules.module_description: In this module, participants learn about artificial intelligence (AI) and generative AI (GenAI) in simple terms. The module explores GenAI's ability to understand, create, and synthesize knowledge based on training data. Examples demonstrate GenAI's capabilities in generating text, images, and engaging in multi-modal interaction, as well as its potential to save time and improve outcomes in government work.

resource_modules.module_description: This module provides a systematic understanding of GenAI's application to public sector work. Participants will learn about ten key areas where GenAI can streamline tasks and be encouraged to experiment with different platforms. The module covers applications such as drafting content, brainstorming ideas, proofreading, summarizing information, role-playing, accelerating learning, coding, analyzing data, and more. A prompting framework with five components (Instruction, Role, Context, Format, and Example) is introduced, along with best practices for simplicity, clarity, flexibility, and efficiency. Participants will engage in hands-on exercises to refine prompts and explore techniques to enhance GenAI interactions.

resource_modules.module_title: Module 5: Overcoming Risks: Your individual use
resource_modules.module_description: This module addresses the responsible use of GenAI by discussing potential risks and mitigation strategies. Participants will learn about data privacy, hallucinations (inaccurate outputs), and bias as key challenges. The module provides practical guidance and organizational policies to assess and avoid these risks, along with strategies to identify and mitigate them. Five crucial behaviors for responsible GenAI use are presented.

resource_modules.module_description: In this module, participants will explore the broader societal risks and uncertainties surrounding GenAI. The module focuses on copyright issues, deep fakes, astroturfing, and the private ownership of GenAI models. Participants will learn about the potential misuse of GenAI for deception, the challenges of identifying AI-generated content in public feedback, and the concentration of power among a few tech companies. The importance of aligning GenAI use with public values and the well-being of communities is emphasized.

Join tens of thousands of learners taking Responsible AI for Public Professionals. 

In today’s digital age, understanding AI is essential for government professionals. Whether improving service delivery or enhancing decision-making, AI can help you tackle public challenges more effectively and ensure your work serves the public.

  • Hands-on Activities: Apply what you learn immediately with interactive exercises
  • Expert Insights: Benefit from a curriculum shaped by leading professionals across government, industry, and academia

  • Professional Recognition: Earn a certificate upon completion to showcase your skills

course_description:
The course is designed for decision makers, organization leaders, and those interested in helping their teams responsibly adopt AI, select and prioritize AI projects.

Learners interested in learning how to use Generative AI in their day-to-day work should look at the other course in this series Using Generative AI at Work. 

Our curriculum design is informed by a sequence of national workshops with federal, state, industry, and academic leaders. You can read more about those workshops and the findings on our website’s blog.
course_learnings:
Through a combination of clear explanations, real-world examples, and practical guidance, the course covers key topics such as:

  • Different AI approaches
  • Selecting and scaling impactful AI projects
  • Ensuring data quality
  • Developing AI talent
  • Navigating ethical considerations and risk management practices

WHO IS THIS FOR

By the end of the course, participants will have a solid foundation for confidently leading their organizations into the age of AI, harnessing its power to improve public services and decision-making while maintaining public trust and promoting responsible AI use.

course_description: Open justice is a growing movement to use new technologies, including big data, digital platforms, blockchain and more, to improve our legal system by making the workings of our legal institutions easier to understand, scrutinize and, we hope, improve. Thanks to new tools the opportunity to make improvements has never been greater. This course is designed to help the public entrepreneur – passionate individuals like you. Whether you are a lawyer, a judge, a technologist or just a concerned citizen – the course will help you to use new technologies to take action to increase efficiency, improve equity, fight corruption and enhance legitimacy in the third branch of government.
course_learnings: Instead of long lectures, this online course consists of ten short modules which will serve as brief introductions to different aspects of open justice. These ‘mini-lectures’ of ten minutes each are combined with interviews with leading practitioners from around the world who are collecting the data, conducting the analysis, creating the apps, and building the movement that helps us all to better know and assert our rights.

course_learnings:
This free, self-paced course equips public servants with the skills needed to plan, run, learn from, and institutionalize meaningful engagement with communities.

WHO IS THIS FOR

Designed for public professionals globally, the course responds to a common challenge in public service: many institutions know engagement matters, but lack clear guidance on how to do it well. Learners gain practical, design-focused skills for running engagement across contexts, including consultation, deliberation, co-creation, and other ways of listening to communities.

MODALITY

Delivered through short, accessible videos, the course focuses on concrete design choices, such as whom to engage, what to ask, and how to use public input in decision-making. Throughout, it shows how artificial intelligence can responsibly support public engagement by reducing time, cost, and complexity while improving accessibility, inclusion, and insight, without replacing human judgment.

PARTNERS

Developed in collaboration with The GovLab and the Allen Lab for Democracy Renovation at Harvard University and a design and advisory board of 50+ global experts on public engagement

WORKSHOP SERIES

The course builds upon the Reboot Democracy workshop series, a set of live sessions on how to design effective and efficient AI-enhanced community engagement that translates public input into meaningful outcomes. Learn more.

AI-POWERED PUBLIC ENGAGEMENT COACH

The course is accompanied by the Public Engagement Coach, an AI-powered tool that helps public servants turn what they learn about engagement into practical action. Learn more.
short_description: This free, self-paced course equips you with the skills to design, run and learn from meaningful engagement with communities.

course_description:
In this free, self-paced course, Anita McGahan introduces a practical framework for driving innovation in government.

You will learn how to design, test, and scale new approaches to public problems—whether through service redesign, new strategies, or collaboration with private and nonprofit partners. Drawing on real-world examples, the course examines how organizations translate promising ideas into measurable impact.

The course also explores how emerging technologies, including AI, fit within broader innovation efforts—alongside process improvements, organizational change, and new forms of partnership.
course_learnings: In this course, Anita McGahan equips public professionals with practical strategies to design, test, and scale innovations—leveraging AI and new technologies and private sector collaboration to improve the public good.
course_title: Driving Innovation in Government: From Ideas to Scaled Impact
short_description: In this course, Professor Anita McGahan equips public professionals with practical strategies to design, test, and scale innovations—leveraging AI and new technologies and private sector collaboration to improve the public good.
short_title: In this course, Anita McGahan equips public professionals with practical strategies to design, test, and scale innovations—leveraging AI and new technologies and private sector collaboration to improve the public good.
course_reasons:
Identify the type of innovation being pursued — Distinguish between workflow redesign, strategic innovation, and structural innovation, and explain why correctly categorizing an initiative is essential to its success.

Recognize the organizational and cultural barriers to tech implementation — Articulate why the primary obstacles to technology adoption in the public sector are human and institutional rather than technical, and apply this understanding when planning an initiative.

Apply appropriate evidence-building strategies — Select and design the right approach to measuring and demonstrating the value of an innovation based on its type, stakeholder concerns, and available resources.

Navigate public-private partnerships effectively — Evaluate potential private sector partners critically, understand the differing strengths and limitations of each sector, and structure collaboration in a way that leverages both.

Develop a realistic plan for growing and scaling an innovation — Anticipate the common failure modes and scaling challenges associated with each innovation type, and design a sequenced approach to piloting, stakeholder engagement, and scaled rollout.
